title: RIS-Empowered Satellite-Aerial-Terrestrial Networks With PD-NOMA
affiliation: Space Engineering University / Henan Polytechnic University / Munster Technological University / University of Thessaly / University of Maryland
domain: SATN / RIS / NOMA / 6G / Physical Layer Security / Resource Allocation

analysis_policy.focus: Extract Summary and Lessons Learned pattern, enumerated challenge structure, three-technology integration approach, per-section conclusion synthesis
analysis_policy.depth: Full paper analysis including basics, performance analysis, applications, and implementation challenges

section_flow.title: Introduction
section_flow.summary: Establishes 6G context, identifies 6 key challenges (fading, connectivity, interference, power, security, hardware), positions survey against 10 existing works (Table I), lists 6 contributions.
key_claims: First comprehensive survey on NOMA-RIS-assisted SATN

section_flow.title: Basics and Applications of SATN, NOMA, and RIS
section_flow.summary: Covers each technology's fundamentals, advantages/shortcomings (Table III), and application scenarios. NOMA comparison figure (Fig. 2), RIS deployment scenarios (Fig. 5-6).

section_flow.title: Motivations and Performance Analysis of NOMA-RIS-Assisted SATN
subsections: C. Three Usage Modes of RIS
section_flow.summary: Explains why NOMA+RIS. Three RIS modes: Reflector, Receiver, Transmitter (Table IV). Two scenarios: SISO, MISO (Table V). Case study with simulation results.

section_flow.title: Resource Allocation for NOMA-RIS-Assisted SATN
section_flow.summary: Two optimization approaches: Mathematical (SCA, SDR, AO, BCD) vs AI-based (DRL, DQN, DDPG). Table VII summarizes references by objectives, variables, algorithms.

section_flow.title: Security of NOMA-RIS-Assisted SATN
section_flow.summary: PLS techniques including secrecy rate, artificial noise, beamforming. Covert communication principles. Passive vs proactive eavesdropping (Fig. 11).

section_flow.title: Applications for NOMA-RIS-Assisted SATN
section_flow.summary: Six application domains with dedicated subsections, each ending with open issues. Comprehensive coverage of emerging technology integration.

section_flow.title: Practical Implementation and Challenges
section_flow.summary: Four main implementation challenges with detailed discussion of each, including STAR-RIS and active RIS considerations.

section_flow.title: Conclusions and Outlooks
section_flow.summary: Synthesizes survey contributions and future directions.

rhetorical_contract.promise: Comprehensive overview of RIS-empowered SATN with NOMA covering basics, performance analysis, resource allocation, security, applications, and implementation challenges
rhetorical_contract.delivery_mechanism: Three-technology foundation → Integration rationale → Resource allocation → Security → Applications → Implementation challenges
rhetorical_contract.unique_contribution: First survey comprehensively integrating NOMA, RIS, and SATN with case study validation and six application domains

synthesis.integration_approach: Three enabling technologies (SATN, NOMA, RIS) combined for mutual enhancement
synthesis.key_paradigm: RIS changes channel environment to make NOMA more effective; NOMA enhances RIS network connectivity

methodology.survey_approach: Technology basics → Integration rationale → Four main technical topics → Implementation challenges
methodology.source_selection: 163 references spanning fundamental to recent works

rhetorical_patterns: Summary and Lessons Learned per major section
Comparison table at end of subsections
characteristic_phrases: The above observations inspire us to...
There are a few critical issues...
However, the assumption of... is unrealistic

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Conclude each major technical section with a dedicated 'Summary and Lessons Learned' subsection synthesizing key insights
structure: First paragraph: Summary of what was covered in the section
Second paragraph: 'Meanwhile/Moreover' lessons learned from the literature
Third paragraph: Critical issues or open problems identified
Use bullet points for itemized lessons if needed
Include forward-looking statements about future research
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Sections III-F, IV-C, V-C, VI-G all follow this pattern with consistent structure
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Provides synthesis at each major milestone; helps readers extract key takeaways without reading full section
reusable_writing_recipes.complexity: Medium - requires synthesis of covered material

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Open introduction with enumerated challenges, then match with enumerated contributions
structure: List challenges as numbered items (1-6 typical)
Each challenge has italic header + explanation paragraph
Later in intro, list contributions as numbered items matching challenges
Each contribution addresses one or more challenges
Use consistent formatting for visual scanning
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Introduction lists 6 challenges (severe fading, weak connectivity, etc.) then 6 contributions addressing them
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Clear problem-solution mapping; demonstrates comprehensive coverage; enables quick scanning

reusable_writing_recipes.description: When surveying integration of multiple enabling technologies, cover each individually then their combination
structure: Section on Technology A basics and applications
Section on Technology B basics and applications
Section on Technology C basics and applications
Section on motivations for integration (A+B+C)
Remaining sections on integrated system topics
Each tech section covers: principles, advantages, limitations, scenarios
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Section II covers SATN, NOMA, RIS individually; Section III covers their integration rationale
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Builds reader knowledge progressively; establishes foundation before complexity; accessible to readers familiar with only one technology
reusable_writing_recipes.complexity: Medium - requires balanced coverage of each technology

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Organize optimization/resource allocation coverage with parallel subsections for mathematical and AI approaches
structure: Subsection A: Mathematical Optimization Algorithm
Subsection B: AI-Based Optimization Algorithm
Subsection C: Summary comparing both approaches
Each subsection covers multiple objectives (rate maximization, power minimization, etc.)
Summary discusses trade-offs: complexity vs adaptability vs optimality
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Section IV uses this exact structure with Table VII summarizing references
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Enables readers to compare approaches; acknowledges multiple valid methodologies; provides guidance for method selection
reusable_writing_recipes.complexity: High - requires deep understanding of both algorithmic paradigms

reusable_writing_recipes.recipe_name: Usage Mode Taxonomy with Per-Mode Discussion
reusable_writing_recipes.description: Categorize technology usage into distinct modes, then provide dedicated discussion for each mode followed by a Discussion subsection
structure: Introduce taxonomy (e.g., three modes)
Subsection per mode with literature coverage
Final Discussion subsection comparing modes
Summary table listing references by mode
Each mode section: principles, applications, limitations, representative references
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Section III-C covers RIS as Reflector, Receiver, Transmitter with Table IV and Discussion subsection
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Comprehensive mode coverage; enables readers to focus on relevant mode; synthesizes cross-mode insights

reusable_writing_recipes.recipe_name: Application Domain Parallel Structure with Open Issues
reusable_writing_recipes.description: Cover each application domain in parallel subsections, each ending with domain-specific open issues
structure: One subsection per application domain (A, B, C, etc.)
Each subsection: motivation, existing works, specific benefits, challenges
Each subsection ends with open issues paragraph
Final Summary and Lessons Learned synthesizes cross-domain insights
Consistent structure enables easy comparison across domains
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Section VI covers CR, BC, MEC, WPT, mmWave/THz, ISAC with consistent structure
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Comprehensive application coverage; domain-specific guidance; cross-domain synthesis
reusable_writing_recipes.complexity: High - requires expertise in multiple application domains

key_concepts.noma_advantage: Enhanced connectivity, high SE, low latency, enhanced fairness via SIC
key_concepts.ris_advantage: Short delay, low energy, simple hardware, long working duration
key_concepts.integration_benefit: Mutual enhancement - RIS changes channels to enable NOMA; NOMA increases RIS network capacity
